choices.english: by 'craftsman' he means Christ the Creator

choices.why: plainer English with the same sense

choices.english: have stirred up love in me

pass_a_gloss: I to Him the faith, and He to me the kingdom. He pastures in the purity of the Scriptures and of the holy doctrines. From those disobeying you, your eyes turn away, and toward me incline; for they, he says, the love stirred up for me [cod. you]. Work of a craftsman: craftsman he names the Creator Christ; for as He became obedient, so the Church. He tells also her chastity and the submission; this soul subjected to faith, the body to chastity. He shows also her priesthood saying: Not lacking mixed wine, clearly the blood of Christ; for this [is] in the hands for the priests. Her neck he calls the deacons of Christ, because [they] carry Christ, the head of the Church. For they carry His holy body in pure conscience, confessing His mysteries.
pass_b_english: I give Him faith, and He gives me the kingdom (Song of Songs 6:3). He pastures in the purity of the Scriptures and of the holy doctrines. Turn your eyes away from those who disobey you (Song of Songs 6:5), and incline them toward me; for they, he says, have stirred up love in me.

'The work of a craftsman' (Song of Songs 7:1): by 'craftsman' he means Christ the Creator; for as He became obedient (Philippians 2:8), so has the Church. He speaks also of her chastity and her submission: her soul is subject to faith, and her body to chastity.

He shows her priesthood too, when he says, 'not lacking mixed wine' (Song of Songs 7:2), that is, the blood of Christ; for this is in the hands of the priests. Her neck (Song of Songs 7:4) he calls the deacons of Christ, because they carry Christ, the head of the Church. For they carry His holy body with a pure conscience (1 Timothy 3:9), confessing His mysteries.
source_text:
λογισμοῖς ἐμποιοῦντος.
Ἐγὼ αὐτῷ τὴν πίστιν, καὶ αὐτὸς ἐμοὶ τὴν βασιλείαν. Ποιμαίνει δὲ ἐν τῇ
καθαρότητι τῶν Γραφῶν καὶ τῶν ἁγίων δογμάτων. Ἀπὸ τῶν ἀπειθούντων σοι τοὺς
σοὺς ἀπόστρε 69.1292 ψον ὀφθαλμοὺς, καὶ εἰς ἐμὲ κλῖνον· αὐτοὶ γὰρ, φησὶν, τὴν
ἀγάπην ἐξήγειράν μοι [cod. σε]. Ἔργον τεχνίτου Τεχνίτην δὲ τὸν δημιουργὸν
ὀνομάζει Χριστόν· ὡς γὰρ ὑπήκοος γέγονεν, οὕτως ἡ Ἐκκλησία. Λέγει δὲ καὶ τὴν
σωφροσύνην αὐτῆς καὶ τὴν ὑποταγήν· τῆς ψυχῆς ταύτης ὑποτεταγμένης τῇ πίστει,
τοῦ δὲ σώματος τῇ σωφροσύνῃ. ∆ηλοῖ δὲ καὶ τὸ ἱερατεῖον αὐτῆς λέγων· Μὴ
ὑστερούμενος κράματι, δηλονότι τῷ τοῦ Χριστοῦ αἵματι· τοῦτο γὰρ τοῖς ἱερεῦσιν ἐν
χερσίν. Τράχηλον δὲ αὐτῆς τοὺς διακόνους τοῦ Χριστοῦ λέγει, διὰ τὸν Χριστὸν
βαστάζειν τῆς Ἐκκλησίας τὴν κεφαλήν. Βαστάζουσι γὰρ αὐτοῦ τὸ ἅγιον σῶμα ἐν

notes: Source checked clause by clause against PG 69 col. 1289-1292.

The row's opening words 'λογισμοῖς ἐμποιοῦντος' are translated at the end of u03-open. The final sentence runs across the row break and is translated whole here; u03-rem-mid begins with the next sentence.
Song verses use English numbering: chapter 6 agrees in LXX and English; in chapter 7 the LXX runs one verse ahead.
The PG column number '69.1292' inside 'ἀπόστρεψον' is print furniture and is not translated.
The source row opens with 'λογισμοῖς ἐμποιοῦντος', the end of the sentence that begins in u03-open; those two words are translated there.
The last sentence runs across the row break ('…ἐν | καθαρᾷ συνειδήσει, ὁμολογοῦντες αὐτοῦ τὰ μυστήρια'); it is translated whole here, and u03-rem-mid begins with the next sentence.

Song verses use English numbering. Chapter 6 numbers are the same in the LXX and English; in chapter 7 the LXX (with the Hebrew) runs one verse ahead (LXX 7:2, 7:3, 7:5 = English 7:1, 7:2, 7:4). 'I give Him faith, and He gives me the kingdom' glosses 'I am my beloved's, and my beloved is mine; he pastures among the lilies' (Song of Songs 6:3); the lilies are read as the purity of the Scriptures.

'αὐτοὶ γὰρ … τὴν ἀγάπην ἐξήγειράν μοι [cod. σε]': PG prints μοι and records the manuscript reading σε ('in you'). The English follows the printed μοι; the variant is kept here in the notes, not in the reader text.

'διὰ τὸν Χριστὸν βαστάζειν τῆς Ἐκκλησίας τὴν κεφαλήν': read as 'because they carry Christ, the head of the Church' (τὸν Χριστόν as object, τὴν κεφαλήν in apposition), which the next sentence ('they carry His holy body') confirms. A reading 'for Christ's sake they carry the head of the Church' is grammatically possible but fits the context less well.
'with a pure conscience … mysteries' echoes Paul's rule for deacons, 'holding the mystery of the faith with a pure conscience' (1 Timothy 3:9).
